chicken-drumstick-baked-coated-skin-coat.title: Chicken drumstick, baked, coated, skin / coating not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks are the lower leg portion of the bird, containing meat, bone and sometimes skin. When baked with a coating they develop a crispy crust, while the skin/coating is usually not eaten.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are used in many world cuisines, from American BBQ to Asian curries.
Baking in the oven retains more nutrients than deep‑frying.
Coatings can be made from whole‑grain flour, breadcrumbs or nut meals, adding extra fiber.
Chicken skin is higher in fat, so it is often removed to lower the calorie count.
Poultry meat is a highly digestible source of protein suitable for most diets.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Drumsticks provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B6, niacin and riboflavin support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health, blood formation and wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes them suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Provides collagen
items.content: Bone and connective tissue contribute a modest amount of collagen, beneficial for skin and joints.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Fat in the skin
items.content: If the skin is left on, the dish can become higher in calories and saturated fat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked meat may contain Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Sodium in the coating
items.content: Pre‑made breading mixes often contain salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you watch sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the drumsticks hot, pulling the meat off the bone. The skin/coating can stay in the dish for flavor but is not eaten. Pair them with vegetable sides, rice, potatoes, or slice cooled meat into salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh drumsticks keep in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Cooked pieces can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat to 75 °C before serving.

ice-cream-cone-scooped-chocolate-waffle-.title: Ice cream cone, scooped, chocolate, waffle cone

content.title: About
content.content: A scoop of chocolate ice cream served in a crisp waffle cone. The ice cream is made from milk, cream, sugar and cocoa, while the cone is baked from wheat flour, sugar and vegetable oil until golden and crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Waffle cones originated in Italy in the early 1920s and quickly spread worldwide.
Chocolate ice cream often contains a small amount of cocoa butter, giving it a smoother texture.
The standard scoop size is about 50 g, providing a balanced portion.
Waffle cones can be slightly sweet or lightly salty, enhancing the contrast with chocolate.
Ice cream cones are frequently topped with sprinkles, nuts, or fruit sauces.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Dairy ingredients supply calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in dairy helps the body absorb calcium more efficiently.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Sugar and fat provide rapid energy, making it a refreshing treat on hot days.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Chocolate contributes flavonoids, which have mild antioxidant properties.

items.title: Mood boost
items.content: Sweet desserts stimulate serotonin production, improving mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience digestive discomfort.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: An allergy to milk or whey requires complete avoidance of the product.

items.title: Nut and gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Waffle cones may contain traces of nuts and gluten, important for those with allergies.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One cone with a scoop can contain 250–350 kcal, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve immediately after preparation to keep the cone crunchy. Add sprinkles, nuts, caramel sauce, or fresh berries for extra flavor variety.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the ice cream in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. Store the waffle cone in a dry place to prevent it from becoming soft. Do not leave the ice cream at room temperature for more than 30 minutes.

content.title: About
content.content: Ensure is a ready-to-drink nutritional beverage designed to support daily dietary needs. It provides a balanced blend of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals, making it a convenient way to obtain essential nutrients anytime.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product was first launched in the 1970s by Abbott Laboratories.
It is available in several flavors: vanilla, chocolate, strawberry, and neutral.
Each 250 ml serving delivers about 20 % of the daily value for vitamin D and over 30 % of the daily value for calcium.
Ensure is frequently used in clinical settings for patients with increased nutritional needs, such as post‑surgery or chronic illness.
The drink requires no preparation – it can be consumed straight from the bottle.

items.title: Supports energy balance
items.content: A mix of fast‑ and slow‑release carbohydrates provides a steady supply of energy throughout the day.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Each serving contains about 10 g of whey protein, which helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B6, and B12 support normal nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Source of calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Helps maintain bone and dental health, especially for individuals with higher needs.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The liquid form is gentle on the stomach, suitable for people with chewing or swallowing difficulties.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some flavors contain up to 20 g of sugar per serving, which may be a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: The product is based on whey protein; those allergic to dairy should choose a non‑dairy alternative.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One serving provides roughly 220 kcal, so it should be accounted for in total daily calorie intake.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: High calcium levels can affect absorption of certain antibiotics; it is recommended to take medicines at least 2 hours before or after the drink.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Keep the shake refrigerated after opening and consume within 48 hours. It can be taken as a standalone meal replacement or as a supplement to regular meals, for example after a workout or before bedtime.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, refrigerate and use within 2 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Pork skin rinds (also known as pork cracklings, chicharrones, or pork chips) are dried and fried pieces of pig skin, often seasoned with salt, spices, or flavorings. They have a crunchy texture and a rich, meaty flavor. The snack is popular in many cuisines worldwide, especially in the United States where it is called pork rinds.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional preparation methods date back to Latin American and Caribbean cuisines.
In the US pork rinds are often marketed as a low‑carb snack for keto diets.
Classic cooking involves boiling the skin first, then deep‑frying it until golden and crisp.
Sweet versions exist, coated with caramel or honey.
In some regions the skins are used as a base for soups and broths.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork rinds contain about 60 % protein, making them a substantial source of amino acids for low‑carb eaters.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: They contain virtually no carbs, which suits keto and paleo dietary patterns.

items.title: Contains collagen
items.content: Collagen from the skin may support joint and skin health, though its bioavailability is limited.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Small amounts of zinc, iron, and phosphorus are present, contributing to metabolic functions.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full for longer.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Most calories come from saturated fat, so consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Many commercial versions are heavily salted, which can raise blood pressure in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Pig meat allergy
items.content: Some people may have an allergic reaction to pork proteins.

items.title: Trans fats from reheating
items.content: Repeated heating of the oil can create trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pork rinds can be enjoyed straight from the bag, added to salads, soups, or used as a crunchy topping for low‑carb dishes. Choose varieties without artificial flavorings and with moderate salt levels.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep rinds in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life store them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard if they develop a rancid smell or off‑flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese ravioli are small pasta parcels filled with creamy cheese and served in a smooth cream sauce. The durum‑wheat dough gives them a firm bite, while the sauce adds a rich, velvety flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ravioli originated in Italy over 800 years ago as a traditional first‑course dish.
Typical cheese fillings combine ricotta, parmesan, and mozzarella, often with herbs.
Cream sauce is usually made from heavy cream, butter, and parmesan, sometimes flavored with nutmeg.
Ravioli are traditionally served as a primo (first course) in Italian meals.
Regional variations exist: Tuscany adds spinach, Piedmont includes mushrooms.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The cheese filling provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese supplies calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the dough and cheese deliver B1, B2, and B6 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Certain cheeses (e.g., ricotta) may contain live cultures beneficial for gut microbiota.

items.title: Balanced carbohydrates
items.content: The pasta provides slowly digestible carbs, helping maintain steady blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cream sauce and cheese can cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The dish is rich in fats and calories, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to milk proteins.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Cream sauces often contain added salt; those with hypertension should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the ravioli hot, drizzled with the cream sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs, grated parmesan, or a light salad. Pairs well with a crisp white wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked ravioli in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Uncooked frozen ravioli can be kept for up to 3 months when vacuum‑sealed.

content.title: About
content.content: Starfruit is the edible fruit of the tropical tree Averrhoa carambola, native to Southeast Asia, Africa and the Caribbean. The fruit has a star‑shaped cross‑section, a crisp texture and a sweet‑tart flavor. It is usually eaten raw, but also used in juices, jams, salads and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The fruit’s shape resembles a star, which is why it is often called “star fruit”.
Starfruit is very high in vitamin C – one fruit provides the daily requirement for an adult.
In some regions the juice is used as a natural pH indicator because it changes color with acidity.
The seeds contain small amounts of toxic oxalates and are generally not consumed.
Traditional Southeast Asian medicine uses starfruit to aid digestion and as an anti‑inflammatory remedy.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity, supports collagen synthesis and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain normal heart function and fluid‑electrolyte balance.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in starfruit help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A medium starfruit provides about 30 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly snack.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Oxalate content may be a concern for individuals prone to kidney stones; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people may experience allergy symptoms such as rash or swelling after eating starfruit.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet varieties can raise blood glucose levels, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wash the fruit, cut it in half and eat the flesh, discarding the seeds. Starfruit can be added to salads, smoothies, yogurts, or used in baking. For a softer texture, lightly grill or bake the slices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store starfruit in the refrigerator in a plastic bag or container, where it stays fresh for up to 1 week. For longer storage, freeze sliced pieces.
